Root cause was the fixture, not the fix: setupRoleTestDB created system_dept as (id, dept_name) with no tenant_id/deleted_at and no rows, so the new ownership check could not validate depts 10/20/30. The fixture now creates the real shape and seeds those departments; the package is green on re-run. Recorded because a reader should know the fix widened the dept-ownership check's blast radius into a second package's fixtures.

Green after two fixes. First run failed: TestRunMigrationsDoesNotReapplyRoleDataScopeBackfillAfterPolicyDeletion builds a scratch database stamped at currentRuntimeSchemaVersion (24) whose system_role has no tenant_id column, so the unguarded INSERT in 000025 failed the whole migration. Two corrections: 000025 now guards on information_schema exactly like 000024 (a database can record 24 while 000024's DDL never ran — the very reason 000024 exists — and there an unguarded INSERT turns startup into a failure loop), and the test's final assertion moved from assertMigrationVersion(currentRuntimeSchemaVersion) to assertLatestMigrationVersion, because the baseline is now deliberately behind the newest file. Its actual claim (a deleted policy is not resurrected) is unchanged and still asserted.

knownGaps: The live installation had no tenant-local role holding a tenant-0 policy, so 000025 inserted 0 rows on pantheon_base. The statement is proven on a scratch database instead (sql-snapshots.txt section D) rather than by production data.

Platform scope (tenant 0) still lists every tenant's roles in the data-scope console. That is deliberate for this wave — the platform administrator is cross-tenant by definition (see hasAdministrativeRole) — but it means the console still shows duplicate role keys to a platform-scoped caller until the W5 viewpoint switcher makes the tenant viewpoint explicit.

A tenant-local role that owns no policy row in its own tenant still fails closed (500 on every governed request). This is pre-existing behaviour, not a W1 regression: 000021 gave every role that existed at the time an `all` row, and roles created afterwards were already policy-less. Inventing a mode here would silently widen a role nobody configured, so it is left to a separate decision.

dept_ids on historical custom policies are copied verbatim. A department id belonging to another tenant can only narrow that tenant's result to zero rows (the row filter is tenant-scoped), never widen it, so it is a correctness wart rather than a leak; new writes are validated.
The frontend permission page's data-scope tab was verified through the browser probe only for the tenant viewpoint; the platform viewpoint is W5.
F14 (cross-tenant role reads answering 500 instead of 403/404) is untouched by W1 and remains unscheduled.
